```{r}

library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(glmmTMB)
library(emmeans)
library(DHARMa)
library(ggplot2)
library (tidyverse)
library (multcomp)
#install.packages("writexl")
library (writexl)
```
Repeated measures on the same plants means we need to account for the within-plant correlation over time. Here's the full analysis:

```{r}

# 1. Load and prepare

df_height<- read_excel("~/Ad_Planta_Trials/Raw_data/Field trial/Field_trial_results_Plantheight_2025.xlsx") %>%
  rename(
    Treatment = Treatment,
    Month     = Month,
    Block     = Block,
    Plant     = Plant,
    height    = `Plant height`
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Treatment = relevel(as.factor(Treatment), 
                        ref = "Non-treated control"),
    Month     = factor(Month, levels = c("May", "June", "July")),
    Block     = as.factor(Block),
    Plant     = as.factor(Plant),
    # Unique plant ID across blocks and treatments
    Plant_ID  = as.factor(paste(Treatment, Block, Plant, sep = "_"))
  )
View(df_height)

# 2. Check data
cat("=== Sample size ===\n")
df_height %>% count(Treatment, Month)

cat("\n=== Height summary by Treatment x Month ===\n")
df_height %>%
  group_by(Treatment, Month) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_h = round(mean(height), 1),
    sd_h   = round(sd(height), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Month, 
              values_from = c(mean_h, sd_h))

# 3. Fit repeated measures mixed model
# Fixed: Treatment * Month (tests growth promotion + temporal change)
# Random: Block (field variation) + Plant_ID (repeated measures)
# Plant_ID accounts for the within-plant correlation across months

m_height <- glmmTMB(
  height ~ Treatment * Month + 
           (1 | Block) + 
           (1 | Plant_ID),
  family = gaussian(),
  data   = df_height
)

summary(m_height)

# 4. Diagnostics
res_h <- simulateResiduals(m_height, n = 1000)
plot(res_h)
#KS test significant (p=0.00026) — residuals deviate from uniform distribution
#Outlier test significant (p=0) — several red asterisks visible at extremes
#Dispersion n.s. — variance is fine, so it's not overdispersion
#The likely causes are the extreme outlier plants 
# Remove flagged outliers
df_height_clean <- df_height %>%
  group_by(Month) %>%
  mutate(
    mean_h  = mean(height),
    sd_h    = sd(height),
    z_score = (height - mean_h) / sd_h
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(abs(z_score) <= 2.5)

cat("=== Rows removed ===\n")
nrow(df_height) - nrow(df_height_clean)

# Refit
m_height2 <- glmmTMB(
  height ~ Treatment * Month +
           (1 | Block) +
           (1 | Plant_ID),
  family = gaussian(),
  data   = df_height_clean
)

res_h2 <- simulateResiduals(m_height2, n = 1000)
plot(res_h2)


```

Extract results
```{r}
# === Q1: Which treatments promote growth vs non-treated control? ===
emm_h <- emmeans(m_height2, ~ Treatment | Month)

contr_h <- contrast(emm_h,
                    method = "trt.vs.ctrl",
                    ref    = "Non-treated control",
                    adjust = "dunnettx")

cat("=== Treatment vs Non-treated control ===\n")
summary(contr_h, infer = TRUE)

# === Q2: Height change between months ===
cat("\n=== Month effect ===\n")
emm_month <- emmeans(m_height2, ~ Month)
pairs(emm_month, adjust = "tukey")

# === Q3: Interaction test ===
m_height_noint <- glmmTMB(
  height ~ Treatment + Month +
           (1 | Block) + (1 | Plant_ID),
  family = gaussian(),
  data   = df_height_clean
)

cat("\n=== Interaction test ===\n")
anova(m_height_noint, m_height2)

# === Letter groupings for plotting ===
cld_height <- multcomp::cld(emm_h,
                             adjust  = "tukey",
                             Letters = letters,
                             alpha   = 0.05) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(
    .group    = trimws(.group),
    Treatment = factor(Treatment, levels = c(
      "Non-treated control",
      "Copper standard",
      "Cons1 (Pb39 and Pb177)",
      "Streptomyces sp. Pb39",
      "Pseudathrobacter sp. Pb177"
    ))
  )

print(cld_height)
#Save y
write_xlsx(cld_height, "~/Ad_Planta_Trials/Outputfiles/Field output files/Plant trial_cld_height.xlsx")


# === Means per Treatment x Month for trajectory plot ===
emm_plot_data <- emmeans(m_height2, ~ Treatment + Month) %>%
  as.data.frame()

print(emm_plot_data)
```


BAr plots
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
p_bar_height <- ggplot(emm_plot_data,
                       aes(x    = Treatment,
                           y    = emmean,
                           fill = Month)) +

  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75),
           width    = 0.7,
           color    = "black",
           linewidth = 0.3) +

  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL),
                position  = position_dodge(width = 0.75),
                width     = 0.2,
                linewidth = 0.5) +

  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "May"  = "#a8d8ea",   # light blue
      "June" = "#4a90d9",   # medium blue
      "July" = "#1a3a5c"    # dark blue
    )
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 230, 20),
    limits = c(0, 235),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +

  labs(
    x       = "Treatment",
    y       = "Plant height (cm)",
    fill    = "Month"
  ) +

  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x      = element_text(size = 10, angle = 45,
                                    vjust = 1, hjust = 1,
                                    face = "italic"),
    axis.text.y      = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.title       = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.text      = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.title     = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    legend.position  = "right",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.caption     = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray40")
  )

p_bar_height

ggsave(
  filename = "Field trial_PlantHeight.tiff",
  plot = p_bar_height,
  path = "~/Ad_Planta_Trials/Outputfiles/Field output files",
  width = 7.5, height = 6.5, dpi = 300, units = "in",
  device = "tiff", compression = "lzw"
)
